newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oil firms nominate blocks in Faroe licence round.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms nominate blocks in Faroe licence round.

text.p: A total of 12 favoured blocks off the Faroes have been nominated by 23 companies for possible exploration licences, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
Statoil is part of the so-called AMG group, which also includes U.S. company Mobil Corp and Enterprise Oil.
The deadline for nominations in the North Atlantic islands' first offshore licensing round was December 5.
The proposed blocks will be considered by the local government-appointed hydrocarbon planning commission, which will draw up regulations for offshore exploration and production.

The commission will report in the next two to three months, with proposals on hydrocarbon planning and general rules for the first round due to be presented to the Lagting, or parliament, in the summer, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Once legislation and regulations have been adopted by the legislature, the Faroese Petroleum Administration (FPA) will invite applications for offshore acreage around December, 1997.
"Since this is our first round, it will take a little time before exploration can start," said Martin Heinesen, head of the FPA.
Heinesen said the FPA would likely require six months to consider applications with acreage being awarded and exploration starting in 1999.
